admission.justification: Text occurrences, duplicate same-line names and undecodable unchanged blobs can otherwise look like unique/current proof definitions, and an unsupported title form can otherwise cost a curator the whole proof. Definition-aware occurrence preservation, honest refusal and a precise line-range alternative prevent false evidence.

applicability: A proof or a citation definition in a JavaScript or TypeScript .test. or .spec. file at the leaf's code candidate: a plain-string case title, an unsupported title form, an undecodable symbol, or a case no path::name reaches.
conditions: A title resolves only from a literal it/test call whose semantic first argument is a plain string; escapes decode and UTF-16 pairs combine while lone surrogate units stay represented.
A bare title bound by more than one call, and an occurrence inside a comment or a non-title argument, is not a unique definition.
An undecodable symbol is unverifiable rather than resolved.

The proof's test carries the case's path and a line_range locator, the anchor records the candidate blob and the content identity of the located bytes, and the evidence pairs with the case's own plain title, bare or behind its plain-titled enclosing describe titles.
Only a case that runs is offered a range; a skipped, todo or otherwise blocking case is refused with its modifier and offered none.
exclusions: The admission of the range as one running case, which the case-extent check decides.
A case whose own title is computed: it pairs with no evidence, and the proof is still written.
statement: Plain-string JavaScript and TypeScript test-case titles resolve as proof symbols with unique bare-title support; invalid UTF-8 symbols are unverifiable; and a case that no name reaches is proved by the exact lines it occupies, while a case that does not run is proved by no range at all.
